articles.title: Stop criticizing your child’s athletic performance on the drive home
articles.summary: Many young athletes are being driven home by parents navigating what to say, if anything. Before you critique their performance, think carefully about your impact.
articles.body: As soon as my son pressed play, the video made me wince. A few years ago, he’d discretely recorded me from the backseat as I was driving, talking to my other son in the passenger seat. We were returning from one of their junior tennis matches and I was questioning what I had perceived to be a lack of effort. As I watched it back, I told myself that it could have been worse; I wasn’t angry but seeing it many years later made me wish I could take it all back. Earlier this summer, I thought about those days again when Melanie Bedard’s 2023 interview with the Toronto Star about “the drive home” resurfaced. Her son Connor was just named captain of the Chicago Blackhawks, and is considered one of the best professional hockey players of his generation. “Connor would say some of his teammates would be crying because they didn’t want to go on the car rides with their dad, with their parents,” she said of his early days in the game. “And I thought, all these people in this machine, you are losing sight of the most important thing, your relation. “Because even if they are the next (NHL hockey legend Sidney) Crosby, they’ll probably be done in their 30s and you’ve damaged that relationship that you could have had for the rest of your life,” she said. How bad is the ‘drive home’? The “drive home” is a recognized experience, almost a rite of passage that many young athletes will have to endure immediately after a disappointing practice or game, trapped inside a vehicle when the emotions are most raw. It’s one of the reasons that many children fall out of love with sports: 70% of youth athletes drop out of organized sports by the age of 13, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics. When I pitched the idea of this story to my editor, his reaction was visceral “I remember those rides home with my dad,” he said, rolling his eyes. Buried in my own subconscious is the memory of my father telling me of his embarrassment when I’d trailed in last place in a 400-meter race at my English middle school. Every season, millions of young athletes are being driven home by parents navigating what to say, if anything, and how to say it. A typical scene was created for a 2016 “True Sport” public service film in Canada: “So, not your best practice,” begins the father’s disappointed monologue as he turns the key in the ignition. “Was something wrong? Because you seem distracted. Can we agree on that?” The camera slowly pans around the car to reveal a young boy sitting diagonally behind him, in silence. “It seemed like you wanted to hang out with your friends more than practice. Maybe we can skip your next game. That way, I don’t have to rush home from work to sit on a freezing cold bench for two hours to watch you and your buddies jerk around.” The put-downs keep on coming, each one cutting deeper than the last, “Wasting your time’s one thing, wasting my time and your coach’s time, that’s selfish. Maybe that’s who you are.” Pushing your child out of sports “The number one reason why kids leave sport is because it’s not fun anymore,” said Karri Dawson, True Sport Foundation’s former executive director. She told CNN that the campaign was designed to speak to the average, well-intentioned parents who may not be aware of the power of their words. In some cases, it was profoundly successful, Dawson said. “They were like, ‘Oh my word!’ People reaching out to me saying, ‘I had no idea that the things I was saying and doing may be having such a negative impact on my child’s enjoyment.’” What plays out in those car rides home has actually been studied by Jeemin Kim, assistant professor of kinesiology at Michigan State University, who worked with the late Katherine Tamminen to understand those conversations. Their findings were published in January 2022. While admitting to a probable sampling bias, because overbearing parents are unlikely to allow GoPro cameras to record their post-game interactions, Kim said that he was generally encouraged by the 28 parent-child pairings and 30 hours of footage he observed. Not all parents are crazy about sports “There’s this narrative of youth sport, parents are crazy, they’re always screaming at their kids, but that just wasn’t the case,” Kim told CNN. The study revealed that 59% of the recording was silence. “When emotions are running high, it’s not a bad thing to sit there and then let the emotions cool down,” he added. The study revealed that sport was only discussed 13% of the time and that parents provided more praise about their child’s performance than the athlete did themselves. “In several instances, parents interjected before athletes could respond to their parents’ comments,” Kim said. Researchers also interviewed the parents and their athlete children. “I remember one kid saying something along the lines of, ‘I love playing the sport, but you don’t play to have these conversations,’” he added. “If that’s the memory they’re going to have associated with youth sport, they’re not going to remember it as good.” Few of us have the wherewithal to be as disciplined as Richard Williams, who famously banned tennis talk with his daughters Venus and Serena on the way home. I remember reading that the father of two of the most famous tennis stars on the planet wanted to preserve the innocence of their youth for as long as possible. It was an edict that applied whether they had won or lost – there would be no recriminations, but he wouldn’t entertain any gloating either. Several US-based organizations have highlighted the ride home as a critical element of a child’s sports enjoyment, but even some of the most vocal advocates admit that it’s not always easy. Former professional soccer player John O’Sullivan, who founded the Changing the Game Project, once admitted that he couldn’t help himself when his son TJ didn’t want to play in the first game for the team that he was coaching. “On the car ride home, I felt the need to address this issue,” he wrote on his website, explaining that his wife karate-chopped him across the chest as soon as he addressed their five-year-old in the back seat. “Really, didn’t you just write a whole book about this?” she shot back with a stern look. It’s an anecdote that many parents will relate to – O’Sullivan was worried that his son would miss out on a game that he had loved all his life. He advises parents now to just to say five words when everyone is back in the car: “I love watching you play.” Regardless of their age, most athletes know when they have messed up. They don’t need to be told. They may also need time to process their own emotions about the game, and a parent’s lecture on the way home may kick off before they’ve fully come to terms with what just happened. Do not analyze your kid’s game The author of several books about peak performance, and a coach of his children’s youth teams, Brad Stulberg understands how consequential these moments can be. “The worst thing you can do is analyze the game,” he told CNN. “And even if they played great, you’re sending a message to the kid, like, ‘Well if I didn’t play great, are you not going to be excited to be with me?’ “I think the kids just want to be kids, and if they want to talk about what happened, they’ll tell you. But generally, my experience is they don’t.” Looking back on those drives with my twins, who are both now in college, our best rides home were the ones that never focused on tennis. On one occasion, as one of my sons was starting to get into music, he’d play a track and ask me to guess how long was left on the song. The first time he asked, I nailed it. Somehow, I knew that there were exactly 27 seconds left on “Wonderwall” by Oasis. His eyes lit up as if I’d just performed some kind of sorcery. It was beginners’ luck, and I never did it again. But it was a magical moment. My boys dropped tennis after high school and are now in a college band together. When they were starting out as budding musicians, the drives home from practice or those early “School of Rock”-style performances were always joyful. There was never any chatter about off-tempo rhythms or missed notes. That’s how I should have done it for sport, too. Nobody wants to be criticized for something that is supposed to be fun, and if you ruin all the fun, don’t be surprised if they don’t want to do it for much longer. Just love watching them play, and talk about anything else.

articles.title: 4 Early Trade Landing Spots for Mark Scheifele Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: It has been a tumultuous offseason for the Winnipeg Jets. Not only have they not made any major additions to a team that went from the Presidents' Trophy to out of the playoffs in one year, but their best and most important player, starting goalie Connor Hellebuyck, has been trying to force his way out of town.
articles.body:
It has been a tumultuous offseason for the Winnipeg Jets. Not only have they not made any major additions to a team that went from the Presidents' Trophy to out of the playoffs in one year, but their best and most important player, starting goalie Connor Hellebuyck, has been trying to force his way out of town.

He not only requested a trade earlier in the offseason, he went public with it as training camp approached, did not report, and is currently suspended while the team works to deal him.

At this point it is just when and where, not if, he gets moved.

If he does get moved it could start a domino effect for the organization and lead to more dramatic changes throughout the roster.

The most potentially significant name that could also be eventually moved: Center Mark Scheifele.

So let's take a look at some teams that could potentially be interested in adding him if Winnipeg did eventually consider a move and put him on the trade block.

Would Winnipeg actually do it, and what would the market be?

The first issue with trying to project a potential Scheifele trade is that it would require Winnipeg to actually be proactive and do something major.

That is simply not how the organization acts under general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff, and has really never acted.

It only makes major moves when its hands are forced either by trade demands or pending free agency, and it tends to take a more methodical team-building approach. Draft and develop, smaller trades and depth free agent signings, and nothing that will rock the boat too much.

Moving Hellebuyck falls under the hands are forced category.

At this point moving Scheifele would have to be a proactive move.

Maybe the departure of a franchise goalie would be an eye-opening move and dictate some sort of a change? Maybe Scheifele would eventually want out himself? It's a lot of hypotheticals and questions.

If it did get to that, Scheifele would be a fascinating player to hit the trade market.

For one, he's a center. Centers always have trade value, even if they are in their 30s.

He is also still really, really good and coming off a career-high 102 point season in 2025-26.

Given that level of production, he is also still really affordable with an $8.5 million salary cap hit for the next five years. With the way the cap is rising, that is a great deal for that level of production.

Will he maintain that level of production into his age 37 or 38 seasons? Probably not. But if you are trying to win a Stanley Cup in the next two or three years, that's probably a player you want.

So with that in mind, let's take a look at four teams that could be a reasonable fit. The list includes a couple of on-the-rise teams, and a couple of contenders that would be trying to keep their windows for contention open a little while longer.

If Scheifele were to become available, the Canadiens should be one of the first teams calling.

They wouldn't need him as a No. 1 center (Nick Suzuki has that spot locked down), but they do need an upgrade at their No. 2 center spot and with their depth down the middle. That might be the one big Achilles heel they have with the roster this season, and Scheifele would give them a pretty dynamic 1-2 punch down the middle.

Montreal is also perfectly situated to make such a move given how much salary cap flexibility it has in the coming seasons due to all of its core players already being locked in to cap-friendly long-term deals. Getting your best players signed for cheap is the type of thing that gives you the flexibility to go out and get the players you still need.

The question here is whether or not Winnipeg would have the willingness to deal him within the division.

Maybe Minnesota has to pay a "division tax," but there would be a definite fit from the Wild perspective.

Center depth is a huge concern here, and has been for a few years during this contention window.

Joel Eriksson Ek is a very good two-way player, but isn't quite the dynamic playmaker and scorer that most championship teams have at the top of their lineup. He might be a No. 2 center posing as a No. 1 center. Adding a player like Scheifele could help him slide down into more of a No. 2/matchup role and give them a more dynamic scorer that could carry the load offensively.

But again, that's a big ask to send him within the division, and Minnesota depleted a lot of its best trade assets a year ago to get Quinn Hughes.

The X-factor here? Minnesota has two really good goalies in Jesper Wallstedt and Filip Gustavsson that could be of interest to Winnipeg after it eventually trades Hellebuyck.

Ranking Top 10 NCAA Men's Hockey Players for 2026-27 Season

On one hand, the Flyers are very clearly in the market for a top-line center. We know this because we saw them try to give Leo Carlsson $15 million per year on a restricted free agent offer sheet over the summer.

Sean Couturier has had a great career in Philadelphia, but he's not a top-line guy anymore.

Trevor Zegras has a ton of talent, but his all-around game is not suited for a No. 1 role, and he might not even be at his best at center.

There is a need, not only for a center, but also for somebody that can just be a difference-maker offensively. As good as they have been defensively over the past few years, generating offense has been a major problem.

Scheifele would obviously help fix that.

The question would be whether or not Scheifele, as a 33-year-old center, would fit into the timeframe the Flyers are currently on. They were a playoff team a year ago, and reached the second round, but it might not be a team that is ready to seriously contend right now. Would Scheifele get them closer to taking a big step?

The Bruins have a lot of players that can play center, and some can do it fairly well.

Elias Lindholm is not a bad player. Pavel Zacha is not a bad player. Fraser Minten had a solid rookie season and has nice upside. James Hagens has the ability to play center if they eventually see him there (he is playing on the wing now).

There is also the reality that Zacha is an unrestricted free agent after this season and might be playing elsewhere after this season, creating another potential opening in the lineup.

The Bruins almost certainly still see themselves as a playoff team, and a team that is capable of contending. But there is always going to be a ceiling on what they can do without a true No. 1 center on the roster. It would not solve all of their problems, but it would solve a big problem.

articles.title: 1 Bold Prediction For Every WWE Title For Rest of 2026
articles.summary: To say the WWE title scenes are super interesting right now would be a gross understatement.
articles.body:
To say the WWE title scenes are super interesting right now would be a gross understatement.

One of the top titles in the entirety of pro wrestling keeps changing hands, after all, going from the likes of CM Punk to Sami Zayn and others.

So-called non-main-event-scene titles currently rest around the waists of fan favorites and/or are embroiled deep in must-see storylines, too.

The result is simple enough: There's an air of importance and unpredictability to most title scenes right now. That's as it should be, of course, but simply hasn't always been the case.

So, let's have some fun with bold predictions around some of the most notable title scenes in WWE right now.

It's easy to think Trick Williams will be coughing up the U.S. title again soon.

This is a title that, after all, rarely has a reign go for more than 50 days, let alone 100-plus. And Williams only won this belt back at Sunday Night's Main Event in September through some silliness involving Lil Yachty.

Even though Williams' feud with Baron Corbin feels over, one can be forgiven for thinking that he won't hold it all that long before it gets hot potato'd around again.

But we're also heading for a quiet portion of the pro wrestling calendar. This might be the stretch Williams holds it while getting built-up, so maybe he'll blow past the 273-day mark set by Logan Paul back in 2023 into 2024.

Bold prediction: Williams sets the longest reign since 2023.

Whereas the main-event titles could use some shorter reigns to keep things interesting, the mid-level titles could use some memorable runs to rebuild their prestige a bit.

Gable got the well-deserved reward for his many, many months of fun storytelling before the unmasking. He's already had some super memorable defenses of the intercontinental title now, too.

By far the best thing WWE can do from here is really take away any and all restraints and just let Gable put on some classics against a wide range of opposition. In fact, him successfully defending it until WrestleMania next year might be a really shrewd move.

Bold prediction: Gable hits the longest reign since Gunther in 2022 (666 days)

The World Tag Team Championships (Austin Theory and Bron Breakker) and WWE Tag Team Championships (Talla Tonga and Tama Tonga) are pretty well-mired in stables action right now.

Fitting, with all the faction drama of Survivor Series on the horizon.

One would think that the belts keep getting passed around a bit, given how much of an afterthought they seem to be at times (did anyone even remember Damian Priest and R-Truth held them for nearly 150 days before The MFTs took them back?).

Same story for the other set of belts, where The Street Profits held it for just 14 days before The Vision took them back.

The bold prediction, then, is both titles stick where they are through the end of the year. Not a lot of reason to keep juggling them around and the focus will be on broader factional drama, so best to have some gold hovering around those scenes.

It feels like WWE wants to really build up Women's Tag Team Champions Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid right now.

The duo took down Brie Bella and Paige, two veterans who initially won the straps at WrestleMania. They then turned around and beat The Bella Twins and Paige in a six-woman tag match at SummerSlam to keep things going.

Right now, the women's tag division doesn't appear to be all that deep. But traditional WWE booking would suggest that some random combination of women aiming for a "bigger" storyline would eventually rip the belts off the current champion.

Let's go the other direction. Fatal Influence, already at a 75-plus-day reign, will keep right on winning, cementing the longest reign past the 177-day record since the belts were established by The Boss 'n' Hug Connection back in 2019.

Bold prediction: Fatal Influence sets new reign record

The Rhea Ripley injury opened the door for Chelsea Green, but she's done more than enough to earn this 60-plus-day reign at the very top.

With retroactive stuff tacked on, Green has technically been top champ since SummerSlam, where she overcame the likes of Charlotte Flair, Jade Cargill and Tiffany Stratton in a ladder match.

That said, it feels like there's an expiration date here. Call it sooner than later, too. Green is already losing to Nikki Bella and others in tag matches on weekly programming.

Look for WWE to get the title on Nikki for "bigger" feuds soon, or for a Cargill-type main-eventer to come take it within the month.

Bold prediction: Green doesn't have much longer as champion

So begins the major redemption arc for Stephanie Vaquer.

Vaquer held the Women's World Championship for 210 days starting roughly one year ago but injuries got in the way. WWE then rewarded her upon her return this month with a shocking win during the WWE South America Live Tour in Santiago, Chile.

A historic, viral moment, it feels like Vaquer is just getting started. She had already achieved the longest run with the belt since 2024, so why not aim even higher?

Think, Rhea Ripley's dominant 379-day run that started in 2023 (which matched a Bayley run from 2019). Poetic, really, that Vaquer should land in that fabled territory. And looking at the roster, great veteran feuds like Asuka, Bayley, Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan don't have any reason to take it from her, either.

Bold prediction: Vaquer one-ups her last reign…by a lot

No reign with the belt is safe right now.

Sami Zayn's last run with the belt lasted nine days. His current one just hobbled over the 20-day mark. CM Punk, Cody Rhodes and Drew McIntyre have all held it since mid-2025, once John Cena coughed it up.

Kevin Owens is next. It just feels right.

Sure, Zayn just beat Owens in a title match on a weekly SmackDown broadcast. But the way this has been going, who's to say the opposite doesn't happen within the next week or two?

This has been a you deserve it title for a while now. And it's stressing to the WWE audience that there's no "skippable" thing on the calendar, even at this time of year and into the winter months.

That lesson is going to pop up soon before the month's out when Zayn hands it off to the next guy.

Bold prediction: Zayn has a matter of weeks, if not days, as champion left

On the other end of this is Roman Reigns, who does not feel like he's going to come close to losing before WrestleMania next year.

Reigns is going to lose to LA Knight at Money in the Bank. WWE has rarely been better set up to take a top title off Reigns. And it's rarely had a chance to do so in a way that helps out so many other people.

Royce Keys' 946 faction is the strongest thing fans have seen since the top Bloodline days. There's nothing better to stress this point than to have them throw interference and cost Reigns his title, fully engulfing him in factional warfare that he's so far steered clear of despite the shocking violence.

There's the LA Knight side of the coin, too. He's more than earned it, so give him the ball and let him run with it for a bit to see how it goes before Reigns takes it back for the run up to WrestleMania.

It's so bold, because at this point, both Reigns and Knight seem so permanently stuck in their respective places.

Bold prediction: Reigns loses to LA Knight

articles.title: Toto Wolff Hunts for Explanation After Mercedes’ Bahrain Drop-Off: “Something Else Is Going On”
articles.summary: The 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was supposed to be a breakout weekend for Mercedes. Armed with a substantial aerodynamic upgrade package projected to...
articles.body:
The 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was supposed to be a breakout weekend for Mercedes . Armed with a substantial aerodynamic upgrade package projected to bring around three-tenths of a second in lap time gains, the W17 looked dominant during Saturday morning's final practice, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli topping the timing sheets.

However, when qualifying arrived, that blistering pace completely evaporated. Max Verstappen stormed to his first pole position of the season for Red Bull, while Antonelli was forced to settle for P4 and George Russell plummeted to P8.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the session, Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff admitted the team was entirely baffled by the sudden loss of performance.

When Sky Sports presenter Simon Lazenby asked what went wrong with the upgraded car, Wolff pointed to bizarre aerodynamic characteristics that haven't plagued the team all season.

"Very difficult to understand," Wolff admitted. "We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn't see all year. But then you can say it's very hot and the tarmac is very different to all the tracks."

Despite the challenging conditions at the Sepang International Circuit, Wolff noted that the team thought they had cracked the setup during FP3. "Looked really good in the morning. You know, we seem to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding," Wolff explained. "And then qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before. Just no performance."

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Friday KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 02: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 leads George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 02, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images)

Further, when pressed on the specific behavioral issues of the W17, Wolff highlighted a crippling combination of straight-line drag and a severe inability to navigate Sepang's technical slow-speed corners.

"I mean, it looks like we are very draggy because it's the first time that we're losing a lot of time on the straights to especially Max," Wolff revealed. "And then through the low speed, we are not able to turn the car. There's just too much understeer. So overall, things we haven't seen all year."

Pundits covering the session speculated that Mercedes might have been purposely sandbagging their true pace. However, when Naomi Schiff asked Wolff if they were hiding performance, the Mercedes boss firmly shut down the theory, insisting a deeper underlying issue was hijacking their highly anticipated aero package.

"No, something else is going on. Something else is going on," Wolff stressed. "And we have to understand, you know, this is now working through the data and putting our heads together because we still believe that the upgrade works. We just need to understand why not here."

With Verstappen on pole and former Mercedes star Lewis Hamilton lining up on the front row in P2 for Ferrari, Wolff and his engineers face a long night of data crunching. If they can't unlock the upgrade's true potential, Antonelli and Russell will face a grueling, defensive race in the punishing Malaysian heat.

articles.title: George Russell explains ‘toughest Saturday of the year’ after poor Malaysia qualifying result
articles.summary: The F1 title contender will start seventh on the grid and was never in contention at the top of the leaderboard
articles.body:
George Russell acknowledged that his disappointing Bahrain Grand Prix qualifying result was his "toughest Saturday of the year" so far.

Russell, who trails Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli by 66 points at the top of the standings with eight rounds remaining, appeared to have flipped the script with his convincing win in Azerbaijan last weekend.

However, the Briton was never in contention at the top of the leaderboard throughout qualifying in Malaysia – hosting the Bahrain GP this year – on Saturday and only qualified eighth-fastest. He will start seventh, courtesy of Isack Hadjar's grid penalty.

With time running out on his championship challenge and with Antonelli starting tomorrow's race in third, a measured Russell admitted his frustration at his first time competing in F1 at the Sepang International Circuit.

"We've struggled today and that is reflected by what was our toughest Saturday of the year," he said. "It is so hot here and the tarmac is very aggressive, with the low grip making lap times several seconds slower than when we last raced here in 2017.

"That may have impacted our performance comparatively to what we have seen at other circuits, but it is true to say that we have clearly suffered more than our closest competitors this weekend. We didn't expect to struggle this much here in Malaysia, and we will work hard to understand why."

Notably, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton – two drivers who have previously raced at Sepang – will start on the front row as the Red Bull driver claimed his first pole position of the season.

"Whilst we are frustrated by our performance today, tomorrow will be a very different challenge," Russell added.

"The race is likely to be dominated by high tyre degradation and keeping the tyres in good shape across a full stint will be the key to a good grand prix.

"Whilst we have ground to make up, we know it should be possible to overtake if you have the speed so we will be giving it our all to make up ground."

Antonelli, meanwhile, said he was satisfied with the second row on the grid after a difficult qualifying session overall.

"I don't think we could have challenged Max (Verstappen) for pole," the Italian said. "He has looked like the quickest car all weekend and so it proved today.

"P3 is not a bad place to be starting from all things considered. The tyre degradation is likely to be very high and, in all probability, it will be a multi-stop race. That will hopefully open up opportunities for us if we have good race pace.

"There is still the possibility of rain too which could make things even more exciting so I'm looking forward to tomorrow."

articles.title: George Russell Baffled by Mercedes’ Malaysian Nightmare: “It Feels Like You’re Driving on Gravel”
articles.summary: Fresh off a massive run on the high-speed streets of Baku, George Russell arrived at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia expecting Mercedes’ highly anticipate...
articles.body:
Fresh off a massive run on the high-speed streets of Baku, George Russell arrived at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia expecting Mercedes' highly anticipated aerodynamic upgrades to solidify their front-running pace. Instead, the British driver found himself staring at a disappointing P8 starting position and a car that felt entirely disconnected from its simulated data.

With track temperatures soaring and the W17 suddenly battling crippling drag and understeer, Russell offered a brutally honest assessment of Mercedes' confusing Saturday slump at the Sepang International Circuit.

When asked by the media if he knew why the weekend had been so much more difficult than the team anticipated, Russell was incredibly blunt.

"No, to be honest," Russell told the media. "Obviously, this circuit is a bit of an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the Tarmac. The lap times seven years ago were about six or seven seconds faster, and at certain points on the track, it feels like you're driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone".

Sepang is historically notorious for its aggressive surface and high lateral tire loads. But while the entire grid is navigating the same challenging conditions, the Mercedes package is failing to cope. "However, it's clearly affecting us more than others," Russell admitted.

A major talking point in the Mercedes garage this weekend is the introduction of a sweeping new upgrade package. Team Principal Toto Wolff previously noted that the team believes the upgrades are working, but unlocking their potential on this specific track is proving nearly impossible.

Russell echoed this frustration, highlighting the brutal reality of trying to validate new parts during a race weekend without the luxury of direct comparisons.

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Friday KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 02: George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 02, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Alex Bierens de Haan/LAT Images)

"That is the big question mark," Russell explained to the media. "If you could have done a direct back-to-back, it would have been great to know. But that's the challenge of this sport. If we'd put the upgrade package on last week, even if it was worse, we probably still would have been on pole, and we'd have been saying it was fantastic".

He also acknowledged the flip side of the engineering coin: "Equally, if we'd had the old car here, maybe the result would have been even worse. So that's the challenge".

When the Numbers Don't Match the Stopwatch

Perhaps the most concerning issue for Mercedes is a dreaded correlation problem. According to Russell, the sensors and data readouts indicate that the new parts are functioning exactly as designed in the wind tunnel, but that performance simply isn't translating to the asphalt.

"As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season, and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us," Russell confessed. "Obviously, as a sport, we need to follow the lap times and not what the numbers say. The numbers look absolutely fine and in line with expectations. However, the result wasn't".

Despite the dismal Saturday showing, Russell remains cautiously optimistic that Sunday's Grand Prix will present opportunities for the team to salvage a strong result. Because Sepang's tarmac acts like sandpaper on the Pirelli rubber, strategy and tire management will dictate the podium.

"The tyre deg is huge, and race pace will be king," Russell concluded. "So, even though today was a real disappointment, it's not the be-all, end-all".

articles.title: Liverpool star scores first international goal in heartwarming moment
articles.summary: Milos Kerkez Delivers for Hungary as Liverpool Role Continues to GrowFor Liverpool, international breaks often come with an understandable degree of anxiety....
articles.body:
Milos Kerkez Delivers for Hungary as Liverpool Role Continues to Grow

For Liverpool, international breaks often come with an understandable degree of anxiety. This one has at least provided a moment to enjoy, with Milos Kerkez delivering a significant milestone for Hungary.

The Liverpool left-back scored the only goal as Hungary defeated Georgia 1-0 at the Puskas Arena, giving Marco Rossi's side a much-needed Nations League victory.

Kerkez struck after 35 minutes, heading Hungary in front following a strong opening from the hosts. Georgia applied pressure afterwards, but Hungary protected their advantage and collected only their second victory in 12 Nations League matches.

Remarkably, this was Kerkez's first senior international goal.

The 22-year-old made his Hungary debut against Germany in September 2022 and has already accumulated 35 appearances. He also became Hungary's youngest player to appear at a European Championship in 60 years when he featured at Euro 2024.

His goal arrived at an important moment. Hungary began their latest Nations League campaign with a 1-0 defeat against Ukraine before drawing 0-0 with Northern Ireland.

Sometimes a defender simply needs to make something happen at the other end of the pitch. Kerkez did exactly that.

Liverpool supporters have become familiar with Kerkez's relentless energy since his arrival from Bournemouth in the summer of 2025.

He made 48 appearances and scored twice during his first campaign at Anfield. Following Andy Robertson's departure, Kerkez has emerged as Liverpool's first-choice left-back under Andoni Iraola.

There is an obvious familiarity between player and coach. Iraola previously worked with Kerkez at Bournemouth, where the Hungarian developed into one of the Premier League's most exciting attacking full-backs and earned selection in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year.

That relationship could prove particularly useful at Liverpool. Iraola knows where Kerkez excels, understands his aggressive approach and, perhaps most importantly, knows how to channel all that energy within a structured system.

Kerkez's career has already covered plenty of ground.

He progressed through clubs in Serbia and Austria before making his senior breakthrough with ETO FC Győr at 16. AC Milan subsequently signed him after Paolo Maldini personally contacted him, although regular first-team football eventually arrived with AZ Alkmaar.

Now Kerkez is establishing himself for club and country. His first Hungary goal represents another landmark in a career which continues to accelerate.

Liverpool will hope there are plenty more still to come.

articles.title: Key matchups for Panthers vs. Lions in Week 4
articles.summary: Can CB Will Lee III put the blanket on one of the NFL's top WRs? Here are our key matchups for Panthers-Lions...
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers will be back on the prime-time stage this Sunday night, when they host the Detroit Lions at Bank of America Stadium. But for them to defy the odds and come out on top, the reigning NFC South champs will have to gain an edge in a number of key matchups.

Here are four battles to keep an eye on here in Week 4 . . .

Panthers HC Dave Canales vs. Lions HC Dan Campbell

With former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson out of the picture in Detroit, the Lions aren't as tough to prepare for schematically as they used to be. However, they still have what may be the best motivational coach in the business in Campbell, who's turned the NFL's longest-suffering franchise into a perennial contender by sheer willpower.

That makes this a really tough matchup for Canales, who's been credited with improving Carolina's culture in the locker room. Now is the time to prove that take is correct. To have any hope at all, Canales has to make the Panthers believe they can beat the Lions— even if they're missing several of their most important players.

Panthers OL vs. Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson

Any upset scenario will require one big change for Carolina—their offensive line has to perform far better than it has so far this season. Going into Week 4, they have allowed the highest pressure rate in the league—and now, they'll face one of the best pass rushers in the league.

Hutchinson will move all around the line of scrimmage—but wherever he's aligned, it's going to take multiple linemen to stop him. If they can't do that, quarterback Bryce Young, as he did in Week 3, is going to have a very long outing.

Panthers CB Will Lee III vs. Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown

On the other side of the ball, the Panthers have some brutal one-on-one matchups—especially at cornerback. Starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, who are both on injured reserve , will not be at Carolina's disposal.

So, Lee may often be lined up across from Detroit's stud wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who has posted 228 yards and five touchdowns in just three games. The good news is that Lee has acquitted himself well, totaling four passes defensed while allowing a 52.6-percent completion rate and a 77.7 passer rating in coverage.

This matchup is a horse of an entirely different color than what he's faced, though.

Panthers LB Devin Lloyd vs. Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs

You could definitely feel Lloyd's absence on the field in last week's loss to the Cleveland Browns . Fortunately, he'll be back in the lineup this week and not a moment too soon.

As their defensive centerpiece and play-caller, Lloyd has to get this unit on better footing against the run—where they're allowing a league-high 193.3 rushing yards per game. Gibbs has racked up 307 rushing yards and 23 first downs to go with six touchdowns from scrimmage—both NFL-bests.

articles.title: What Travis Kelce’s Chiefs teammate told him privately as retirement question lurks

articles.body:
How much longer Travis Kelce has left in the NFL remains a big topic of discussion after he returned for Year 14 of his career.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has made an electric start to the 2026 season having put up 231 receiving yards and two touchdowns through the opening three weeks. Which is a really promising sign given the regression seen in his stats over recent years.

What lies ahead in the season in terms of fitness remains to be seen, but Kelce is looking as good as ever in the Chiefs' offence, which is firing on all cylinders following the addition of running back Kenneth Walker III.

After Kelce's encouraging start to the season, teammate Noah Gray has revealed what he has privately told the star tight end about how good he is looking on the field this season.

Travis Kelce's Chiefs teammates stunned by his age-defying fitness

The Chiefs are heading into their Week Four game against the Las Vegas Raiders, with one of the AFC West teams set to lose their unbeaten record on the season. Kelce will be expected to play a big role, with Gray admittedly left so impressed with his start to the year.

"He's awesome. He's flying around. I told him the other day, "Looked like he was 27." He is a great leader. He's a guy that comes in to work. He's another extremely humble dude, always willing to help out with whatever you need. He's just a guy that uplifts you," he told the media.

"When you show up to work and you got a guy like that, a leader like that, in the locker room, it makes you want to go out there in practice even when you don't want to."

Kelce turns 37 years of age on Monday, which naturally brings his future in the game under scrutiny. It has been a busy year for the tight end following his marriage to global superstar Taylor Swift back in July.

However, with the Chiefs' offence looking so much more functional through the addition of an actual running back threat in Walker, it has allowed Kelce and Patrick Mahomes to get back to their best form through these early weeks.

Whether Kelce still has the hunger for another season is something only he can answer, but it is clear that he is looking as fit as ever to his teammates.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Publicly Humiliated By His Own Fans On Friday Night.

Boy oh boy.... we all expected the reception to be a frosty one, but this may have exceeded even the expectations of the most fanatical Dylan Larkin haters.

On Friday night, the hometown hero turned captain who became a disgraced pariah in the City of Detroit in just the span of a single summer had to face the music in front of his home crowd at Little Caesars Arena and boy was that music as loud as could be.

articles.title: Why Mercedes' Bahrain GP upgrade is still a "big question mark"
articles.summary: Championship-leading team puzzled by "things we haven't seen all year" after applying major update package in Malaysia
articles.body:
The Mercedes team has taken a big swing by introducing a substantial aerodynamic update package at a circuit Formula 1 hasn't visited since 2017. Has it missed?

Probably not – but, because the upgrade is a major one, Mercedes has committed to it on both cars so it has been unable to run back-to-back comparisons between old and new in identical conditions. This has added to the challenges of understanding why the W17 seems to have coped notably poorly with the Sepang track's abrasive asphalt surface.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli set the fourth-fastest time in qualifying after a mistake in Q2 meant he needed to use another set of the Pirelli C4 soft tyres, leaving him with just one remaining for Q3. George Russell was eighth fastest, though both Mercedes drivers will gain a place on the grid owing to Isack Hadjar's engine penalty.

"That is the big question mark," said Russell when asked by Motorsport.com if the team had found it difficult to extract the potential of the new package.

"If you could have done a direct back-to-back it would have been great to know, but that's the challenge of this sport. "If I put the upgrade package on last week, even if it was worse, we probably still would have been on pole and we'd have been saying it was fantastic. And equally, if we had the old car here, maybe the result would have been even worse. "So that's the challenge. As a team we have yet to have, let's say, a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us."

The entire sidepod profile of the W17 has changed, as has much of the architecture underneath

The Mercedes upgrade features a new floor with major revisions to the leading edge, diffuser, and furniture around the rear wheels. More significantly it adopts a very different sidepod profile which it's understood has required the internal cooling architecture to be redesigned.

For this reason it is not possible to swap between the two specifications during a race weekend.

What has really provoked puzzlement within the team is the W17's apparent aversion to the unusually rough track surface at Sepang. It is highly unlikely to have been caused by the upgrade package, but it hinders efforts to understand and optimise it because there is no equivalent data set for the previous spec.

"It's very difficult to understand," said team boss Toto Wolff.

"We've been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn't see all year. But then you can say it's very hot and the tarmac is very different to all the [other] tracks.

"It looked really good in the morning [when Antonelli topped FP3 by 0.278s from Max Verstappen, who later qualified on pole]. We seem to have at least with Kimi made a step in understanding.

"And then qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before. Just no performance.

"It looks like we're very draggy because it's the first time we're losing a lot of time on the straights, especially to Max. And then through the low speed, we are not able to turn the car. There's just too much understeer.

"So overall, things we haven't seen all year."

Antonelli's qualifying was compromised by a track-limits violation in Q2

Antonelli and Russell certainly appeared to go backwards relative to their competition between final practice and qualifying. Russell was 0.741s off Verstappen's pole time despite having the typical two runs on new tyres in Q3.

Championship leader Antonelli had a lap struck off in Q2 for a track-limits violation, requiring him to go again with a new set of tyres which had originally been destined for him to use in Q3. That left him with just one opportunity to go for a push lap in Q3 because the C4 hasn't proved resilient enough at Sepang to do more than one.

All the drivers have had to contend with a low-grip surface which is highly abrasive, owing to the more open nature of the aggregate. This has been a feature of the circuit ever since it was opened in 1999; the intention was to make the surface less slippery when wet, and to drain and dry quicker after bouts of rain.

"Obviously this circuit is a bit of an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac," said Russell. "The lap times seven years ago were about six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you're driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone. However, it's clearly affecting us more than others.

"All the numbers say it's [the upgrade] an improvement, but obviously it's a sport where we need to follow the lap times and not what the numbers say. So the numbers look absolutely fine and in line with expectations.

Henry comments on an Eric Bieniemy video

Eric Bieniemy is the offensive coordinator for the Kansas City Chiefs and has been in the league for over two decades. Henry, who has no affiliation with him, was seen talking at a press conference and shared a comment that many found hilarious.

"D*** I look good in red!" wrote Henry on X

Bieniemy was addressing the media as the Chiefs prepare for their next game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Both teams are 3-0, making this a game of huge importance.

The OC did not reply to Henry's comment, but it is a comparison due to the physical similarity between the two. Bieniemy was a running back during his playing days, which means he was explosive, a quality Henry used to possess during his time wrestling.

Borussia Dortmund has made a request to the Greek national team to spare Konstantinos Karetsas in their game with Germany.

Karetsas started in all three of Greece's Nations League matches including in the historic win against Germany, playing the full 90 minutes.

According to Sky Germany, Dortmund has therefore reached out to and requested that the 18-year-old BVB talent be used sparingly.

The Westphalian club's concern probably comes from Karetsas recently shouldering a heavy workload for the club.

He also suffered from circulatory problems before the international break and will face Werder Bremen with Dortmund next Friday.

It leaves Greece with a tricky call given Karetsas is one of their star player and they currently sit top of Group B with 7 points.

Roethlisberger puts Rodgers' CBS coverage in focus

Ben Roethlisberger sparked a fresh conversation about CBS's coverage of Aaron Rodgers after the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals. During his Footbahlin show, the former Steelers quarterback questioned how often CBS cameras focused on Rodgers during the game.

His comments added another layer to the discussion surrounding Rodgers and Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Here's a closer look at what happened on the field and what Roethlisberger said afterward.

Roethlisberger discussed television shots of Rodgers during Pittsburgh's Bengals game. He said Rodgers is shown frequently when frustrated and stated that CBS shows him more than other quarterbacks.

Those remarks came during the September 29 Footbahlin episode, which reviewed Pittsburgh's divisional victory. The episode also discussed the offensive line, running game, defense, and several plays that influenced the final result.

operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos

Rodgers delivered three touchdown passes

Rodgers had a stronger statistical performance against Cincinnati after Pittsburgh scored only 3 points in Week 2. He completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards, averaging 8.6 yards per attempt with a 101.6 passer rating and 3 touchdowns.

His touchdown passes went to Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and DK Metcalf. Rodgers also had 3 rushing attempts for 10 yards as Pittsburgh produced 411 total yards in the victory.

Pittsburgh produced 411 total yards against Cincinnati, including 273 passing yards and 138 rushing yards. The total marked a substantial increase from the Steelers' 235-yard offensive output against New England in Week 2.

Jaylen Warren led Pittsburgh with 127 rushing yards on 17 carries and added 49 receiving yards. His 176 total yards were the Steelers' highest individual yardage total in the game.

CBS televised the Steelers-Bengals game on September 27 at Acrisure Stadium. The Pittsburgh broadcast team featured Ian Eagle on play-by-play and Ross Tucker providing analysis.

The matchup came during Rodgers' second season with Pittsburgh after he returned to the Steelers in 2026 on a one-year contract. His continued presence remained a major subject of coverage surrounding the team.

The criticism focused on camera attention

Roethlisberger's criticism centered on how often CBS cameras showed Rodgers' reactions during the game. He said the quarterback appeared angry during broadcasts and argued that CBS repeatedly returned to those moments.

His comments were his own observation rather than a statement from CBS. Available reporting does not provide a statistical count comparing Rodgers' screen time with other quarterbacks during the Bengals game.

Rodgers delivers three-touchdown performance

Rodgers finished the Bengals game with 3 touchdown passes and 1 interception. He was sacked twice and completed 19 of 34 attempts while Pittsburgh matched Cincinnati's scoring throughout much of the afternoon.

His touchdown passes helped Pittsburgh remain within reach after Cincinnati repeatedly answered. Boswell eventually supplied the winning points with a 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining in regulation.

Interesting fact : Roethlisberger was selected 11th overall in the 2004 NFL Draft by Pittsburgh after playing at Miami University in Ohio.

Cincinnati took a 27-24 lead with 13:29 remaining in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh then answered with a late scoring drive after an 87-yard Warren run was erased by a holding penalty on Metcalf.

Rodgers connected with Darnell Washington for 47 yards during the drive. Warren added a 26-yard run before Boswell kicked the go-ahead 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining.

Interesting fact : Ben Roethlisberger's 2018 season was one of his biggest statistical years, as he threw for 5,129 yards and 34 touchdowns while starting all 16 games.

Pittsburgh's final scoring possession covered 77 yards after the Steelers lost Warren's long run to a holding penalty. Rodgers completed passes during the drive, allowing Boswell to attempt the go-ahead field goal.

Cincinnati had one final opportunity, but Derrick Harmon sacked Burrow and forced a fumble with 44 seconds remaining. Sebastian Joseph-Day recovered the ball near midfield, ending the Bengals' final possession.

operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos/Depositphotos

The Bengals entered Week 3 with a 2-0 record after victories over Tampa Bay and Houston. Pittsburgh was 1-1 after beating Atlanta and then losing 20-3 to New England.

Rodgers improved his numbers against Cincinnati after the Week 2 defeat. Against New England, he completed 23 of 39 passes for 187 yards, 0 touchdowns, 1 interception and a 60.5 passer rating.

Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and 3 touchdowns against Pittsburgh. His scoring passes included a 28-yard touchdown to Tee Higgins late in the first half.

Ja'Marr Chase caught 9 passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, while Higgins had 6 receptions for 90 yards. Cincinnati took a 27-24 lead in the fourth quarter before Pittsburgh eventually regained the lead.

The comments followed a busy game review

Roethlisberger's comments came during the September 29 episode of Footbahlin, which reviewed Pittsburgh's Week 3 win. The episode also examined the Steelers' offensive line, Warren's production, defensive issues, and the team's upcoming Thursday game.

CBS's postgame coverage separately featured Ross Tucker, Bryant McFadden, Terron Armstead, and Ben DiNucci discussing the Bengals matchup. The network's coverage therefore continued beyond the live broadcast.

The conversation around former NFL players and major football moments also includes Brian Urlacher drawing a 'line in the sand' over Kaepernick protest .

Pittsburgh finished Week 3 at 2-1 after defeating Cincinnati, while the Bengals also moved to 2-1. Pittsburgh then lost 27-24 to Cleveland on Thursday, Oct. 1, dropping the Steelers to 2-2.

Roethlisberger's remarks created additional discussion about Rodgers' television coverage after the Bengals victory. The documented point is that he criticized the frequency of Rodgers-focused shots during CBS's broadcast.

The broader NFL discussion also turns to player behavior, including Jason McCourty calling for the NFL to crack down on flopping after Broncos' win .

articles.title: Is Vanderbilt QB Jared Curtis playing against Georgia football?
articles.summary: Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis, who decommitted from the Georgia Bulldogs, is a game-time decision
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs (4-0) will face the Vanderbilt Commodores (3-1), who are led by Jared Curtis a major Georgia flip at quarterback. Unfortunately, Curtis's health status has been up in the air, with Friday's injury report listing him as questionable. His status will be updated 90 minutes before kickoff (12:45 p.m. ET kickoff time on Saturday, Oct. 3). According to ESPN's Pete Thamel, Curtis will be a game-time decision.

"Curtis will attempt to play on Saturday, with a final decision to come after he's evaluated pregame," tweeted Thamel . "Curtis has been limited all week in practice but made it through Friday walk-through without issue."

Curtis has dealt with a short-term, undisclosed injury throughout this entire week. He played every snap in the 21-15 loss to Auburn , so either he was playing through the injury or he sustained it in practice. If he misses the game, Vanderbilt will more than likely turn towards Blaze Berkowitz, who has 178 yards, no touchdowns, and no interceptions so far.

Curtis, a five-star quarterback from the class of 2026, was known for infamously flipping from Georgia to Vanderbilt on the first day of the early signing period. With Heisman candidate Diego Pavia running out of eligibility, Curtis put himself in a position to start right away. After a few games, the Commodores named him the unanimous starter.

In his first start, Curtis went 20 of 34 for 277 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. He helped Vanderbilt to get an exciting 35-31 win over N.C. State where a Wolfpack fumble in the end zone won it on the last play. In his next game against Auburn, he didn't shine as much: 199 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. He has 746 yards, four touchdowns and three interceptions on the year.

articles.body:
Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the upcoming Shanghai Masters, the men's world number one in tennis said on Instagram on Saturday.

"Unfortunately I won't be able to play at the Rolex Shanghai Masters this year as I had hoped. I always enjoy playing in front of the Shanghai fans and I'm very sorry that I won't be able to do so next week. Thank you for all your support. I'm looking forward to seeing you again next year!" he wrote.

Sinner has been out of action since his Wimbledon triumph in July due to a knee injury.

The Italian won the Shanghai trophy in 2024, when he defeated Novak Djokovic in the final.

This year's Shanghai Masters will take place on October 7-18.
